doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: Union card troubles with Locals 208 and 802
summary: Dropped from the Chicago local, Ware is stopped from working, is fined for cursing the delegate, and complains about dual cards.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Yeah. And I couldn't gig around because I was buying (inaudible) and dropped my local Chicago card -- I was 802, behind me about 6 months in my dues, 208 and they wouldn't let me work, and I had some gigs around town I could have worked. I worked up on the North Side with a guy named Spider. Spider was the drummer out of Pittsburgh that was playing at a little club called the French Poodle up near the North Side. And he had Dodo Marmarosa Mamarosa in tow. Dodo was playing piano, I was playing bass and Spider was playing

drums. In come the delegate. 'Boy, you know you ain't supposed to be on that bandstand.' And I said, 'Man, well, how do you expect me to make it then?' -- and blah, blah, blah. He was gonna have me up before the Board, and I went down there, and I went off; I screamed, and they wound up getting me fined. I had to pay a fine to the International for cussing them out. Grey was the President of the black local. You know, it was just a thing with them; I had to kiss their ass in order to work, you know, and I had gone to the local ever since I come out of the service, you know, but I dropped my card when I moved to New York; I dropped my Chicago card. I said what's the use of holding two cards, you know. Although some cats do. Some cats have their home town card and then get New York cards, too.

In fact, that's what you're supposed to do -- but it don't make sense to me. I figured that once you've gone to the American Federation of Musicians, one card should allow you to work all across the country.
Or anywhere in the world, really.

Well, it does in certain times, certain circumstances. You can go in there so long as you pay the local tax to the local union. But I say if you're doing a week, you got to pay them so much percent on your earnings to that local, and that's all right, but you know, to me it's kind of grafty, but you had to do it to work. And, you're

only gonna be there a week, you know, I mean -- but it's a necessary evil. If you just stay that long, you got to wait to establish residence, and you can't work for six months, by your waiting to pay your money to join that local.
